title: Synthesis of Niobium(V)‐Stabilized Tetragonal Zirconia Nanocrystalline Powders
authors: Jagadish C. Ray; Asit B. Panda; Chitta R. Saha; Panchanan Pramanik
journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

steps.description: ZrOCl2·0.8H2O, NH4OH, oxalic acid, and ammonium oxalate are used to prepare solution A of (NH4)2Zr(C2O4)3 via Zr(OH)4·xH2O.
Nb2O5, HF, ammonium tartrate, and H2O2 are used to prepare niobium tartrate solution B via H2NbF7.
Solutions A and B are mixed in proper ratios to form niobium-ion-containing zirconium oxalate solutions with 5, 10, 15, and 20 mol% Nb5+.
PVA is added to form precursor solutions with a molar ratio of metal ions to PVA monomer of 1:0.5.
The precursor solution is evaporated and pyrolyzed over a hot plate for about 4 h at a bed temperature of ~250°C to form the precursor material.
The precursor material is calcined at different temperatures (600° to 1700°C) to form nanocrystalline powders of niobium-ion-doped ZrO2.
